labels.name: terminal

body: **Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?**: Yes - VS Code Version: code-oss (latest) - OS Version: Debian Linux (x86_64) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Install code-oss on Debian Linux 2. Launch code-oss from terminal 3. Attempt to open the Terminal panel ## Description VS Code (code-oss) fails to launch the integrated terminal due to an outdated libnode.so dependency. When Node.js is updated on the system, the installed libnode version becomes newer than the version that unixTerminal.js expects, causing the terminal to crash. The issue manifests when: - System libnode is updated to a newer version (e.g., libnode.so.120) - code-oss still references the old version (e.g., libnode.so.115) - Terminal attempts to load and system cannot find the expected library version ## Expected Behavior Terminal should launch successfully and allow command execution, or gracefully handle version mismatches by linking to the available system libnode version. ## Actual Behavior Terminal fails to initialize and causes a system crash (physhost crash) due to library version mismatch. The process crashes when unixTerminal.js attempts to load a libnode version that doesn't exist on the system. ## Error ``` Error: libnode.so.115: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory ``` ## Workaround I've documented a temporary solution using symbolic links: https://gist.github.com/CyberMan571/f98d6c633db2f5ed522015b782603265 **Temporary Fix:** ```bash # Find the installed libnode version ls -la /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnode.so* 2>/dev/null || ls -la /usr/lib/libnode.so* # Create a symbolic link to the newer version # Replace XX with your installed version number (e.g., 120) sudo ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnode.so.XX /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnode.so.115 ``` ## Root Cause The `unixTerminal.js` module has a hard-coded dependency on a specific libnode version. When the system's Node.js library is updated, this binary dependency is no longer satisfied, causing terminal initialization to fail. ## Proposed Solution 1. Update unixTerminal.js to dynamically detect and link against the available system libnode version 2. Implement version compatibility checking during terminal initialization 3. Provide a fallback mechanism for cases where exact version match is not found ## Additional Context This issue affects users on Linux systems that receive Node.js updates, particularly on rolling-release distributions like Kali Linux. The hard-coded dependency prevents terminal usage until manual intervention is performed.

body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes ### Environment - VS Code: 1.130.0 - Built-in npm extension: v1.0.1 - npm: 12.0.1 - OS: Windows 10 ### Description Using npm 12.x.x, hovering over a dependency in `package.json` shows only "Installed version". The output for a single package is `[{...}]` rather than `{...}`. The affected method is `PackageJSONContribution.npmView()` in `extensions/npm/src/features/packageJSONContribution.ts`: ```typescript private async npmView(npmCommandPath: string, pack: string, resource: Uri | undefined): Promise { const args = ['view', '--json', '--', pack, 'description', 'dist-tags.latest', 'homepage', 'version', 'time']; const stdout = await this.runNpmCommand(npmCommandPath, args, resource); if (stdout) { try { const content = JSON.parse(stdout); const version = content['dist-tags.latest'] || content['version']; return { description: content['description'], version, time: content.time?.[version], homepage: content['homepage'] }; } catch (e) { // ignore } } return undefined; } ``` When npm 12's `npm view --json` outputs `[{...}]`, `JSON.parse(stdout)` produces an array. Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327169

- Add `onDidReplaceNewDraftSession` for the workspace New Session → New Session lifecycle, distinct from draft graduation.

title: Incrementally refine dictation transcripts
body:
Fixes #327222
Fixes #327219

## Summary

- periodically refine stable portions of the live dictation transcript instead of waiting until recording stops
- send at most 800 trailing characters per incremental request, with a five-second minimum interval
- preserve the previously refined display prefix while keeping the raw ASR transcript untouched for final cleanup and fallback
- cancel stale or overlapping refinement requests when dictation stops, is cancelled, or speech recognition revises the processed prefix
- reject cleanup output that adds or rewrites dictated words, preventing requests from being followed as instructions or turned into generated HTML/code
- ask post-processing to format dictated sequences as Markdown bullet or numbered lists

## How incremental cleanup works

While the user dictates, VS Code periodically sends a stable portion of the recent transcript to the cleanup model. During active transcription it leaves the newest 20 characters untouched because speech recognition may still revise them; after one second without an update, the complete live tail is considered stable, including short dictation. Cleaned text appears while recording continues. If speech recognition revises processed words, stale cleanup is cancelled and retried. When recording stops, the complete raw transcript receives the existing authoritative final cleanup pass.

Both incremental and final cleanup are controlled by `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup`. Disabling the setting turns off both behaviors.

The final cleanup retains its timeout, cancellation, length limit, output-faithfulness validation, and raw-transcript fallback behavior.

body:
Depends on #327211.

The language-model cleanup added by #327211 runs only after dictation stops. For longer dictation sessions, we could improve responsiveness and reduce the final cleanup latency by periodically refining only the trailing portion of the transcript while the user is still speaking.

## Proposal

- Periodically reprocess only the trailing **N seconds** of dictation, or the **last sentence**, rather than sending the full transcript on every update.
- Keep the earlier, already-refined prefix stable so text does not churn while the user dictates.
- On each refinement, replace only the matching trailing segment with the cleaned result.
- Preserve the existing final cleanup pass when dictation stops, including its cancellation, timeout, length-limit, and raw-transcript fallback behavior.
- Avoid overlapping refinement requests; a newer trailing segment should supersede stale work.

## Goals

- Show punctuation, casing, and filler-word cleanup during dictation.
- Reduce perceived latency when dictation ends.
- Bound model input and request frequency for long sessions.
- Prevent partial or stale model responses from corrupting the transcript.

## Open questions

- Whether the refinement boundary should be time-based, sentence-based, or a combination of both.
- What interval and trailing-window size provide the best quality/latency tradeoff.
- Whether incremental cleanup should remain behind `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup` or have a separate experimental setting.

title: Voice: don't auto-send the turn by default when hands-free is disabled
body:
Fixes #327217

## What

When hands-free mode (`agents.voice.handsFree`) is **disabled**, voice mode no longer auto-sends the turn by default. Previously the turn ended automatically on trailing silence (`agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`, default `800`) and on a stop phrase (`agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`, default `['send it']`) regardless of the hands-free setting, which is surprising for users who opt out of the automatic back-and-forth loop.

## How

In `voiceClientService._getTurnConfig()`:
- Read `agents.voice.handsFree`.
- When hands-free is disabled, suppress trailing-silence ending unless `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs` is **explicitly** configured, and suppress stop-phrase ending unless `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases` is explicitly configured (via `IConfigurationService.inspect()`).
- Users who explicitly set either setting keep that behavior; the derived `auto_end_mode` becomes `off` only when nothing opts in.

Also:
- Re-send the turn config to the backend when `agents.voice.handsFree` changes (previously only silence/phrase changes triggered a resend).
- Update the setting descriptions for `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`, `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`, and `agents.voice.handsFree` to document this.

## Notes

- No behavior change when hands-free is enabled (the default), or when the turn settings are explicitly configured.
- Draft.

title: Chat custom endpoint: API key stored with trailing newline, causing 403 on all requests

labels.name: insiders-released

body:
## Summary

When configuring a custom LLM endpoint in VS Code, the API key is stored in SecretStorage with a trailing `\n`, causing every request to fail with a 403.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Copy an API key from a terminal — e.g. `op item get my-api-key --field credential --reveal | pbcopy`. The clipboard includes a trailing newline (standard shell behaviour).
2. Open VS Code and configure a custom endpoint via the Chat model picker or `chatLanguageModels.json`.
3. Paste the key into the input dialog and press Enter to confirm.
4. VS Code stores `key\n` instead of `key` in SecretStorage (`chat.lm.secret.*`).
5. Every request to the custom endpoint fails: `403 token expired or invalid`.

## Expected behaviour

VS Code should trim whitespace (at minimum `\n` / `\r\n`) from the API key value before calling `context.secrets.store()`.

## Why this is not user error

Pressing Enter is the **only** way to confirm the input dialog — users cannot avoid it. Trailing newlines in clipboard content are ubiquitous (shell commands, password managers, terminal copies all append `\n`). The fix is a single `.trim()` call on the stored value; the burden should not be on the user to strip the newline before pasting.

## Workaround

Strip the newline before copying to clipboard:
```bash
op item get my-api-key --field credential --reveal | tr -d '\n' | pbcopy
```

## Environment

- VS Code 1.130.0 (darwin arm64)
- Custom endpoint via `chatLanguageModels.json` with `${input:chat.lm.secret.*}` reference
- Confirmed by inspecting `state.vscdb` — the decrypted secret contains a trailing `0x0A` byte

## Suggested fix

In the custom endpoint configuration flow, before storing the secret:
```ts

title: Experimental: clean up dictation transcript with a language model
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327205
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327204

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d0d5525-9840-4104-910a-4d66d051a9db

## Clean up dictation transcript with a language model

Our built-in on-device dictation (streaming Nemotron ASR via Foundry Local) emits lowercase, largely unpunctuated text and transcribes filler words verbatim, so dictated input reads as one long run-on. The underlying model and the Foundry SDK expose no punctuation option, so this runs the final transcript through a small language model to restore formatting.

### How it works
- Setting **`dictation.experimental.llmCleanup`** (on by default, experimental).
- After the raw transcript is produced, `ChatSpeechToTextService.stopAndTranscribe()` sends it once to `copilot-utility-small` (via `ILanguageModelsService`) with a strict "only fix punctuation, casing, spacing, and paragraphs; preserve wording; drop fillers/false starts; never answer" prompt, then returns the cleaned text.
- Robust and non-blocking:
  - Owns a per-cleanup `CancellationTokenSource` with a 10s deadline; cancelled from `cancel()`. If the session is aborted mid-cleanup, `stopAndTranscribe()` bails without touching shared state, so it can never get stuck in `Transcribing` or tear down a newly started session.
  - Transcripts over the 4000-char cap skip cleanup and return raw (no truncation).
  - The response stream is consumed with strict error propagation and `await response.result`, so only a complete response can replace the transcript — a mid-stream failure falls back to the raw transcript.
  - `finalizeMs` telemetry is measured after cleanup so it reflects model latency.

### Gating
Programmatically gated on Copilot: with AI features disabled, `selectLanguageModels` returns none and cleanup is skipped, falling back to the raw transcript.

Describe the feature you’d like

When an MCP server requires model access (for example, to perform sampling), VS Code should explicitly notify the user if the currently selected model has not been granted permission to be used by that MCP server.

Currently, this failure is difficult to discover. From the user’s perspective, the MCP server appears to be malfunctioning, even though the actual issue is simply a missing model access permission.

This is especially confusing because:

* The MCP server starts successfully.
* The server is visible in VS Code.
* Tools may even be listed correctly.
* There is no obvious indication that the selected model is not allowed to access the server.

As a result, many users naturally assume that:

* the MCP server is broken,
* OAuth or authentication is misconfigured,
* or the MCP implementation itself has a bug.

Only users who already know about Configure Model Access are likely to identify the real cause.

Expected behavior

Instead of failing silently, VS Code should provide a clear and actionable message such as:

This MCP server is not permitted to use the selected model.

Actions could include:

* Grant Access
* Configure Model Access

or automatically open the model access configuration dialog.

Why this would help

The current security model makes sense—requiring explicit permission before an MCP server can use a model is a reasonable default.

The issue is discoverability, not security.

A clear permission prompt or error message would significantly improve the onboarding and debugging experience while preserving the existing security model.

Instead of spending time debugging a perfectly healthy MCP server, users would immediately understand that the missing permission is the only issue.

body:
Fixes #327205

## Improve built-in dictation punctuation and remove filler words

Our on-device dictation (streaming Nemotron ASR via Foundry Local) emits lowercase, largely unpunctuated per-segment text, and transcribes speech disfluencies verbatim. The result reads as one long lowercase run-on sentence full of "um" and "uh".

Both apply to live finalized updates and the final `stop()` transcript. Always on, since the raw output is objectively worse. The interim (shimmering) partial tail is left raw and re-normalizes when it finalizes.

### Tests
Added `localTranscriptionService.test.ts` covering run-on splitting, short-pause joins, no double-punctuation, "i" → "I", null-timing fallback, filler stripping/variants, filler-only segments, and preservation of filler-like real words.

**The problem**  
Currently, if a user pins a Markdown preview tab, editing another \.md\ file causes the preview to switch to the new file, ignoring the \pinned\ state. This contradicts user expectations, as pinning should lock the content.

**The solution**  
Added a check in \onDidChangeActiveTextEditor\ within \preview.ts\:

- **New private method** \#isTabPinned()\: Gets the webview's \iewColumn\ and checks if the corresponding tab has \isPinned === true\.

- **Guard**: If \#isTabPinned()\ returns \	rue\, the handler returns early, preventing the preview content from being replaced.

1. Pinned preview + edit another file → **Preview does NOT change**.

title: Chronicle cost tips: parity with CLI /chronicle cost-tips
body:
Adapts the highest-value recommendation-quality improvements recently made to the Copilot CLI `/chronicle cost-tips` into the VS Code chronicle skill. Preserves existing VS Code Chat scoping, cloud/local backend gating, slash-command behavior, security constraints, and telemetry attribution. Does not touch the `sessionStoreSql` API and does not introduce a deterministic profile API in this change — that's a separate follow-up.

## What changes

`extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/chronicle/SKILL.md` — replaces the freeform "Step 3: Provide tips" section under `### Cost Tips` with a fixed report contract:

1. **`## Top cost drivers`** — required, must appear before any recommendations. 3-5 material patterns, most-impactful first, each with rough numbers and an evidence class:
   - `exact` — grounded in cloud `events` fields `usage_input_tokens` / `usage_output_tokens` / `usage_model` on `assistant.usage` rows.
   - `proxy` — inferred from local turns, checkpoints, session_files, tool_requests, or message lengths only. No real token numbers.
   - `mixed` — labeled per-driver when a report combines both.

   Explicit token or cost claims require **exact** evidence. Proxies stay described as proxies — turn counts, checkpoint gaps, and message lengths never get translated to tokens or dollars.

2. **`## Recommendations`** — **at most 3**, ordered by expected impact. Each recommendation:
   - Ties back explicitly to a named driver above (no recommendation without a matching material driver).
   - Is directly actionable in VS Code Chat: model picker, `/compact` (or a fresh chat when compaction isn't available), narrower task framing / smaller working sets, subagent delegation, reusable `.github/copilot-instructions.md` / `.github/skills/` / `.github/agents/` entries — only when a repeated pattern justifies it.
   - Ends with two separate lines: `Expected impact:` (quantify only when evidence is `exact`) and `Confidence:` (`high` / `medium` / `low`).
   - Does not copy Copilot CLI–only commands or Coding-Agent–only workflows.

3. **`## Data caveats`** — required disclosure so the user can weigh the report: backend/source (cloud DuckDB / local SQLite / mixed), time window, in-scope `agent_name` values + session count, and fallback/precision limits (e.g. "no per-event token data on local", "cloud store empty in window", "percentages omitted — grand total not computable").

### Additional guardrails baked into the prompt

- Percentages are only allowed against a real **period grand total** (sum of in-scope `usage_input_tokens + usage_output_tokens`). Never against a truncated top-N sum. If the grand total can't be computed, the percentage is dropped and called out in caveats.
- Context-growth findings ("input tokens keep climbing turn-over-turn") gated at **`>=50%`** late-vs-early input-token growth, inclusive. Smaller growth is explicitly called noise and must not be listed.
- Attachments are treated as neutral work artifacts. Attachment presence alone is not waste — only concrete evidence of the same attachment / file being repeatedly ingested when it did not need to be counts as a driver.

### Sparse / insufficient data

Hardened so the model doesn't invent findings when the store is thin:

- Still fills out `## Data caveats`.
- Skips `## Top cost drivers` or leaves it as "No material drivers observed in this window."
- Offers **no more than 2-3** clearly labeled `General habit — not observed in your data:` items, anchored to VS Code chat features (model picker for routine work, `/compact` or fresh chat on long sessions, reusable instructions when a workflow starts to repeat). No arbitrary hard thresholds.
- For local-only users, still closes with the `chat.sessionSync.enabled` upsell.
- Explicit "Never fabricate specific sessions, files, models, token counts, or percentages" clause.

## Preserved behavior

- Default VS Code Chat scoping (`'VS Code Chat'` on cloud, `'GitHub Copilot Chat'` on local, with the mix-check offer to widen to `Copilot CLI` / `Copilot Coding Agent` / subagents on request).
- Cloud vs local backend gating (local SQLite has no `events` table; token-level analysis requires cloud sync).
- `chat.sessionSync.enabled` upsell for local users.
- Slash-command routing (`/chronicle cost-tips`) and existing Step 1 (Investigate) / Step 2 (Map to features) guidance.
- `sessionStoreSql` tool API is untouched. No deterministic profile helper in this change — deferred by design.

## Tests

`extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/test/sessionStoreSqlTool.spec.ts` — the existing `'chronicle SKILL.md Cost Tips section carries required anchors'` test is extended with anchors for the new contract markers so the shape stays pinned without overfitting the whole prose:

- Section anchors: `## Top cost drivers`, `## Recommendations`, `## Data caveats`
- Recommendation shape: `at most 3`, `Expected impact:`, `Confidence:`
- Evidence classes: `**exact**`, `**proxy**`, `**mixed**`
- Guardrails: `period grand total`, `>=50%`, `neutral work artifacts`, `General habit — not observed in your data:`, `Never fabricate`

## Validation

- Manual full-file scan against the extended assertion list — all 24 required anchors present in the updated SKILL.md.
- Could not execute the vitest suite or the repo `precommit` hygiene hook in the authoring environment: the private npm feed (`packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io`) is unreachable from this machine so root `node_modules` cannot be populated (`event-stream` missing when `node build/hygiene.ts` runs). Structurally the diff is hygiene-safe by construction — `build/filters.ts` excludes `extensions/copilot/**` from `indentationFilter` and excludes `**/*.md` from `copyrightFilter`, and neither file's copyright header, tab indentation, or existing code style was modified. CI on this PR should be the real signal.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Apply the same evidence-class / expected-impact / confidence discipline to the `### Tips` (non-cost) workflow in the chronicle skill.
- Introduce a deterministic profile helper on `sessionStoreSql` (top drivers, grand-total computation, sparse-data flag) that the prompt can consume instead of asking the model to hand-roll aggregates every time.
- If the CLI adds further guardrails after this snapshot (e.g., stricter model-mix definitions, explicit anti-patterns for archiving-style tips), fold them in as a subsequent commit.

Steps to Reproduce:

## Description

The MCP Servers section presents valid same-name collisions as indistinguishable duplicate rows. The flattened Agent Host projection loses parent provenance and uses the child flag without the parent container flag. Same-name workbench configurations also show the same label/description, making valid collisions look like accidental duplicates.

## Root Cause Analysis

Exact server name is a collision key, not identity. The Customizations list flattened top-level and container-backed Agent Host MCP entries without carrying the parent container. It therefore could not display plugin/directory provenance or compute the documented effective state `container.enabled && server.enabled`. Separately, same-name workbench rows did not show their MCP configuration origin.

title: Agents session disappears after switching away from a failed session with an active fork

labels.name: bug

labels.name: papercut :drop_of_blood:

body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.59.2026072302
- VS Code Version: 1.131.0-insider (9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04, arm64)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window, Copilot CLI multi-chat/forked chat, Sessions sidebar
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Reproduced and correlated in local Agent Host, AHP, renderer, and profile-storage logs. Relevant event sequence and conclusions are included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In the Agents window Sessions filter, leave **Failed** unchecked (the persisted profile value is `sessionsListControl.excludedStatuses = [4]`, where `4` is UI `SessionStatus.Error`).
2. Open a Copilot CLI session and let its default/main chat fail.
3. Fork the chat before the failure point and continue working in the fork so the peer chat is actively `InProgress`.
4. Observe that the active session remains visible in the sidebar, but its row is labelled **Failed** even while the fork is running.
5. Switch to another session.
6. Observe that the original session immediately disappears from the Sessions sidebar.
7. Re-enable **Failed** or reset the Sessions filters; the session reappears.

## Expected

A running peer/fork chat should promote the aggregate session status to `InProgress`, matching the Sessions contract (`NeedsInput > InProgress > other`). Switching away should therefore leave the still-running session visible when only Failed sessions are excluded.

See - https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C09MVCZKLP4/p1784823824073999?thread_ts=1784823693.032779&cid=C09MVCZKLP4

## Actual

The aggregate session remains `Error` while the peer chat is running. Because Failed sessions are excluded, the row is visible only while active and disappears as soon as another session becomes active. This looks like destructive session loss, although the session, chats, and worktree are still present.

## Root Cause Analysis

There are three interacting behaviors:

1. `AgentHostStateManager._aggregateChatSummaries` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts` checks `errorChat` before `inProgressChat`, giving the effective precedence `InputNeeded > Error > InProgress`. When the default chat has failed and a peer fork starts streaming, the session summary therefore remains `Error`.
2. `SessionsList.update` in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts` filters sessions whose status is in `excludedStatuses`.
3. The same method deliberately reinserts a filtered session while it is active. Once the user switches sessions, that exception no longer applies and the Error-status session vanishes from the list.

The multi-chat status implementation conflicts with `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`, which documents `NeedsInput > InProgress > other`. Existing tests cover a running peer with an **idle** default chat, but not a running peer with an **errored** default chat.

## Log Evidence

- The default chat transitioned to protocol `Error`.
- The forked peer chat subsequently transitioned to protocol `InProgress`.
- No aggregate session-summary transition to `InProgress` was emitted while the fork ran.
- A later `listSessions` response still contained the session with `Error | IsRead`; there was no delete, archive, or dispose request.

## Suggested Fix

Change the aggregate precedence to `InputNeeded > InProgress > Error`, then add a regression test where:

1. the default chat is Error;
2. a peer chat starts and the session becomes InProgress;
3. the peer completes and the session falls back to Error.

A secondary UX improvement would be to make active status filters more obvious, since the active-session exception currently masks the filter until navigation.

title: fix: guard undefined stdio command in MCP server identity (fixes #327148)
body:
### Summary `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')` thrown from `McpServer._hasUnresolvedVariables` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpServer.ts:745`). The MCP policy-governance layer builds an `IMcpServerIdentity` from a stdio launch via `_identityFromLaunch` as `command: [launch.command, ...launch.args]`. Although `McpServerLaunch.Stdio.command` is typed `string`, discovery/config producers assign it directly from untrusted configuration (e.g. `pluginMcpDiscovery._toLaunch` and `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters` use `command: config.command` / `command: server.command`). When a user's stdio MCP entry omits `command`, that value is `undefined`, so the produced `identity.command` array contains an `undefined` element — violating `IMcpServerIdentity.command: readonly string[]`. The new policy check `_hasUnresolvedVariables` then calls `arg.includes(...)` on that `undefined` element and throws inside the reactive `_policyBlock` autorun during `McpService.updateCollectedServers`. Fixes microsoft/vscode#327148 Recommended reviewer: `@vijayupadya` ### Culprit Commit `e1b18379` — "Add enterprise allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers governance policies for MCP servers" (PR #326226) by `@vijayupadya`, milestone 1.130.0 (matches the reported regression version). This PR introduced the identity-based policy matching flow (`_identityFromLaunch`, `_hasUnresolvedVariables`, `_policyBlock`) that first calls `.includes()` over the identity command elements. Before this feature an `undefined` stdio command never reached a string method on this path. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[MCP config/discovery omits 'command'] --> B[McpServerLaunch.Stdio.command = undefined
despite typed string] B --> C[_identityFromLaunch builds
command: [undefined, ...args]] C --> D[_policyBlock derived autorun] D --> E[_hasUnresolvedVariables] E --> F["identity.command.some(arg => arg.includes(...))"] F --> G[TypeError: reading 'includes' of undefined] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpServer.ts` — `_identityFromLaunch` produces the `IMcpServerIdentity` whose command array is consumed by the policy check. ### Repro Steps 1. title: Agents window repeatedly prompts for MCP authentication after extension host restart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released

body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in
- VS Code Version: 1.131.0 main at `3d97feaadbd`
- OS Version: macOS
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window, local Agent Host, Copilot provider
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Model-independent
- Logs: Agent Host debug export inspected locally; relevant sanitized timeline and AHP facts are below

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure an OAuth-protected remote MCP server that uses dynamic client registration, such as Notion at `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`.
2. Create an Agents window session using the local Copilot Agent Host. Send a message so the MCP servers start.
3. In the response, select **Authenticate** in `The MCP server notion requires authentication. Authenticate?` and complete authentication. Confirm that Notion reaches `ready`.
4. Create another session without restarting the extension host. The remembered grant is silently reused and no authentication prompt appears.
5. Restart the local extension host, or reload the window.
6. Create another Agents window session and send a message.

## Expected

The persisted dynamic OAuth client registration, token, account preference, and MCP access grant are restored non-interactively. Notion should become ready without showing another authentication prompt.

## Actual

Every session created after the extension-host restart reports Notion as `authRequired` and shows the Authenticate prompt. Selecting Authenticate once recreates the provider and makes all currently loaded Notion sessions ready, without requiring a new OAuth login.

## Evidence

All timestamps below are normalized to UTC:

- `11:20:11`: local extension host pid 94024 starts.
- `11:20:25`: Notion returns a 401 OAuth challenge and the session reports `MCP server 'notion' requires authentication`.
- `13:02:35`: the dynamic Notion authentication provider is registered and `MCP authentication succeeded for notion`; the Notion MCP client initializes.
- `13:06:34`: a later session starts in the same extension-host lifetime without another Notion prompt.
- `13:48:21`, `13:48:37`, `13:48:47`, and `13:49:11`: the local extension host restarts.
- `13:49:27`, `13:50:42`, `14:08:55`, and `14:17:35`: each newly started session again reports Notion as requiring authentication.
- `14:17:57`: selecting Authenticate causes four AHP `authenticate` RPCs and all four loaded Notion sessions transition to ready.

The Notion `authRequired` payload has `oauthClient: undefined`, `authorization_servers: ['https://mcp.notion.com']`, and no required scopes. This is the dynamically registered OAuth path, not the configured/static-client path.

A separate `Eng MS` server also fails with HTTP 403 and a `VPN REQUIRED` response in this capture. That is independent of the Notion persistence failure. File watcher `EMFILE` errors may have contributed to extension-host instability, but a clean extension-host restart is sufficient to expose the provider-restoration gap.

## Root cause analysis

`AgentHostSessionHandler` silently checks auth-required MCP servers by calling `resolveMcpServerAuthentication` with `allowInteraction: false`.

For explicit/static OAuth clients, `resolveMcpServerAuthentication` obtains `IDynamicAuthenticationProviderStorageService` and can restore a matching persisted provider. For Notion, `oauthClient` is undefined, so the storage service is not obtained. `getOrCreateProviderForMcpResource` instead calls `IAuthenticationService.getOrActivateProviderIdForServer`.

`getOrActivateProviderIdForServer` only considers currently registered providers and manifest-declared providers. After the extension host restarts, the dynamic Notion provider is neither active nor declared, even though its client registration and tokens remain persisted. The lookup returns undefined; because the operation is non-interactive, `getOrCreateProviderForMcpResource` refuses provider creation and returns undefined. Silent authentication therefore returns false and the session surfaces the prompt.

The interactive Authenticate path calls `createDynamicAuthenticationProvider`. Its extension-host delegate reloads the persisted client registration and tokens, which explains why the server becomes ready without a real login.

PR #326736 restored persisted providers for configured/static OAuth clients, but its logic is entirely inside the `oauthClient` branch. PR #326881 added session-wide silent MCP authentication and therefore exposes this remaining dynamic-registration gap consistently.

## Proposed direction

Permit non-interactive rehydration only when the deterministic dynamic provider ID already has a persisted, usable client registration. Recreate the provider with that stored client ID/secret, then require the existing account preference and MCP server URL access grant before forwarding a token. Do not perform fresh dynamic client registration, rotate an invalid client, prompt for client credentials, create a new login session, or update consent during the silent path.

Add regression coverage for:

1. An inactive persisted DCR provider with an allowed existing session is restored and its token forwarded without interaction.
2. No persisted registration means no metadata fetch, provider creation, DCR, or prompt.
3. Invalid-client/token-refresh failure remains non-interactive and leaves the Authenticate card visible.
4. Configured public/confidential OAuth client behavior remains unchanged.
5. Concurrent post-restart sessions restore the provider once.

title: [Bug] Secondary Side Bar Webview resize starves Windows input for over 30 seconds
body:
## Summary

Dragging the width sash of a VS Code Secondary Side Bar containing an OpenChamber Webview can cause severe intermittent input stalls on Windows. The sash may move only once or twice per second, then pause again. The interaction can remain in this state for more than 30 seconds before returning to normal responsiveness.

## Reproduction

1. Move the OpenChamber extension view into the Secondary Side Bar.
2. Open a complex chat session containing long Markdown and a Mermaid diagram.
3. Drag the Secondary Side Bar width sash continuously.

A simpler OpenChamber session has much less severe lag under the same interaction.

## Expected behavior

The sash should track pointer movement continuously, and VS Code should continue processing mouse input during the resize gesture.

## Actual behavior

Mouse input is starved during the resize gesture. The sash moves intermittently, sometimes only once or twice per second, with repeated pauses. The stall can last longer than 30 seconds.

## Environment

- Windows
- VS Code 1.127
- Electron 42.2
- OpenChamber Webview hosted in the Secondary Side Bar

## ETW evidence

A Windows ETW capture of the complex session shows `Code.exe` Browser main thread (`CrBrowserMain`, TID 20372) consuming `23.249s` CPU during a `25s` resize window.

- CPU-sampled stacks predominantly enter the Windows USER path: `Code.exe -> win32u.dll -> win32k.sys -> win32kfull.sys`.
- Windows UI Delay reports that Browser main does not check messages for `19.110s`.
- `Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND` receives a `WM_MOUSEMOVE` after an additional `1.078s` delay.
- In the simpler-session ETW capture, the maximum message-check delay is `3.672s`.

The Browser main thread receives CPU for nearly the whole abnormal interval. The trace therefore does not indicate ordinary scheduling starvation or a blocked wait. Current ETW symbols do not identify the specific `win32kfull` function, so I cannot determine whether the work originates in VS Code Webview hosting, Electron/Chromium embedded-content handling, or Windows window management.

Renderer, GPU, extension-host, DPC/ISR, and hard-fault evidence do not account for the over-30-second input stall. OpenChamber Mermaid content creates a separate Webview rendering task before the resize, but it does not execute during the Browser main input-starvation window.

## Related reports

- OpenChamber investigation and trace context: https://github.com/openchamber/openchamber/issues/2388
- Related but unconfirmed as the same cause: #254179. That report covers macOS whole-window resize lag with a visible Webview; this report covers Windows Secondary Side Bar sash dragging and prolonged input starvation.

## Attachments

The two ETW captures are each approximately 1.6 to 1.7 GB, so I am not attaching them directly to GitHub. I can provide the captures on request. The OpenChamber issue above contains the related trace investigation context.

title: Add dictation backend selection; support for using MAI; rename dictation settings
body:
## Dictation backend selection + settings cleanup

Adds a cloud dictation backend option and regroups the dictation settings under a generic `dictation.*` namespace, since these settings govern dictation across chat, editor, and terminal — not just chat.

### Settings

| Old | New | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.speechToText.model` | `dictation.model` | Renamed; adds a cloud **`mai`** option alongside the on-device Nemotron model. |
| `chat.speechToText.enabled` | `dictation.enabled` | Renamed to a generic dictation kill-switch. |
| `chat.speechToText.mode` | _(removed)_ | The shortcut now always uses the former `auto` behavior: tap toggles, hold is push-to-talk. |

Settings migrations map any stored `chat.speechToText.*` values (including legacy on-device model ids) to the new keys, preserving an already-configured destination value (e.g. after settings sync) and clearing the removed `mode` key.

### Backends

- **`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b`** (default): on-device, via `ILocalTranscriptionService` (Foundry Local). Offline; no audio leaves the device.
- **`mai`**: cloud, via `IVoiceClientService` — the same voice service Voice Mode uses. Streams PCM16 over the voice websocket (PTT), authenticated with the GitHub token. Requires network + sign-in.

Selecting `mai` routes dictation start/stop/audio through the voice client instead of the local transcription service; nemo remains the default.

**Shared-connection safety** (the voice socket is a single connection shared with Voice Mode):
- Refuses to start when the socket is already connected, and only disconnects a connection this dictation established — so dictation and Voice Mode can't tear down each other's session.
- Requires GitHub sign-in (fails with an actionable message) before connecting rather than opening an unauthenticated socket.
- Filters transcription events by `turnId` and drops non-increasing `revision`s, so a late/other-turn event can't corrupt the transcript or resolve the final waiter early.
- Subscribes to `onFatalDisconnect` (terminal close codes 4001/4008/4029, e.g. another window took over) and fails/tears down the session — closing the mic — with a user-facing message.

### Telemetry (backend comparison)

The goal is to A/B compare the two backends, so dictation emits two events sliced by `backend` (`nemo` / `mai`) and `surface` (chat / editor / terminal).

**`chatSpeechToText.session`** — usage, reliability, and latency:
- `timeToFirstTranscriptMs` — first streamed audio → first transcript; isolates backend transcription latency (excludes mic acquisition + model download).
- `finalizeMs` — stop → final transcript; the post-stop wait.
- `partialUpdates` — count of interim (non-final) updates; a churn/stability proxy.
- plus existing `outcome`, `segments`, `transcriptLength`, `errorCode`.

**`chatSpeechToText.accuracy`** — a ground-truth-free accuracy proxy: how much the user edits dictated text before sending it. After a dictation finalizes, the dictated span is followed with a tracked decoration; the diff is measured at the **actual submit** (a `notifyDictationSubmitted` hook in the chat input part and the Agents composer send path, before the editor clears), falling back to clear/teardown otherwise:
- `dictatedLength`, `editDistance` (Levenshtein), `editRate` (`editDistance/dictatedLength`, capped at 1; lower is more accurate), `edited`, and `submitted` (whether an actual send fired vs. a clear/teardown).

Only aggregate character metrics are logged — never any transcript text. Edits typed at the span's edges are excluded so unrelated appended text isn't counted.

Examples (`editRate` = `editDistance / dictatedLength`, capped at 1):

| Scenario | dictated → submitted | editDistance | editRate | edited |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clean, sent as-is | `add a retry to the upload handler` → _(same)_ | 0 | 0.00 | false |
| One misheard word fixed | `fix the of by one error…` → `fix the off by one error…` | 1 | 0.03 | true |
| Mostly rewritten | `um open the setting is file` → `refactor the parser` | 22 | 0.82 | true |

Across many sessions, a better backend shows more `edited=false` and lower `editRate` on the rest; `submitted=true` rows are the trustworthy signal.

### Notes

- Whether the MAI backend requires an explicit `sendStartSession` before PTT transcription still needs verification against a live backend; draft until validated end-to-end.

title: gen_ai.agent.name never reflects the active custom agent for top-level (non-subagent) sessions
body:
Copilot Chat's OTel export (`docs/monitoring/agent_monitoring.md`) documents `gen_ai.agent.name` as required on `invoke_agent` spans and the `copilot_chat.agent.*` metrics. In practice, for a session where the user has directly selected a custom `.agent.md` agent (not one dispatched via `runSubagent`), this field is always the generic `"GitHub Copilot Chat"` — including for `copilot_chat.session.start`, `copilot_chat.agent.turn.count`, and `copilot_chat.agent.invocation.duration` — never the actual persona's name.

Confirmed against a real 22,950-line/242MB capture: zero occurrences of a directly-selected custom agent's real name anywhere in the file, across every `session.start` event. Subagents dispatched via `runSubagent` *do* get real names in the same file (11k+ occurrences), confirming the identity-threading mechanism exists — it's just not wired up for the foreground/top-level case.

Root cause, from source (as it stood in the former `microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat` repo, prior to archival — same logic should now live under this repo's Copilot Chat extension code): `provideCustomAgents()` (e.g. `githubOrgCustomAgentProvider.ts`, the local-file equivalent) returns bare file URIs, not distinct `vscode.ChatParticipant` registrations — VS Code loads the `.agent.md` content as a persona layered onto one fixed shared participant (`editsAgent`, see `chatAgents.ts`). `emitSessionStartEvent()` (`genAiEvents.ts`) derives `gen_ai.agent.name` from that participant, so every directly-selected custom agent collapses to the same generic identity regardless of which persona is actually active.

This is also user-visible in a confusing way: the agent will correctly self-report its real persona name in chat if asked directly ("Which agent are you?" → "JARVIS"), since that's a prompt-layer fact the model has — but that identity never makes it into the telemetry layer.

**Ask:** thread the active custom agent's real name into `gen_ai.agent.name` for top-level/foreground sessions too, not just `runSubagent`-dispatched ones — the persona is already known internally (it's driving the system prompt and tool list), it's just not being surfaced to the OTel identity fields.
